props.title: Black Sabbath

sections.content: Mario Bava's Black Sabbath (1963) revolutionized anthology horror with three masterfully crafted tales of terror. The film's most famous segment, "The Drop of Water," creates unbearable tension through its use of color and sound, influencing later horror classics like Deep Red (1975) and Suspiria (1977). Boris Karloff's magnetic presence as host and star of "The Wurdulak" segment bridges the gap between Universal's classic monster era and the more visceral Italian horror movement of the 1960s.

sections.content: The film's influence extends far beyond horror anthologies. The psychedelic lighting techniques Bava pioneered in "The Drop of Water" segment became a hallmark of Italian horror, reaching their apex in Dario Argento's Phenomena (1985) and Inferno (1980). The band Black Sabbath even took their name from this film, cementing its place in pop culture history. Bava's innovative use of handheld cameras and extreme close-ups in the "The Telephone" segment influenced found footage horror decades later.

What sets Black Sabbath apart is its sophisticated approach to horror psychology. Unlike the monster movies of its era, Bava delves into human nature's dark corners. This psychological approach influenced Roman Polanski's Repulsion (1965) and modern art-horror like The Witch (2015). The film exists in two versions - the Italian cut emphasizes supernatural horror while the American version, recut by AIP, leans into psychological terror. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Anthology Horror

movies.title: Lisa and the Devil
movies.slug: Bava's surreal masterpiece about a tourist lost in a mysterious villa. Features Telly Savalas in a devilish role.

sections.content: Black Sabbath established conventions that later anthology films would follow. Creepshow (1982) adopted its host-introduced format, while Tales from the Darkside: The Movie (1990) borrowed its twist ending approach. Modern anthologies like V/H/S (2012) and XX (2017) continue drawing from Bava's playbook of using different directors or styles for each segment while maintaining thematic coherence.
